messages:
Michael: heads up — acme-prod escalation. Their SRE reports a ~3x p99 regression on /v1/embeddings starting after last kernel rollout (kernel-v1.9-ffa3c). p95 looks fine. They say tail is worst for sequences >1024. sample req ids shared in DM.
Sara: which model variant? any change to quantization or batching?
Michael: model=redwood-3b-embed, quant=8bit, batching unchanged. compile flags: -O3 -march=native -DUSE_FLASH_ATTENTION (from CI artifact).
Alex: thanks. I'll try to repro locally with same kernel + flags. If FlashAttention path regresses for long seqs we might be picking an inefficient kernel for those shapes.
Matt: quick mitigation: we can flip the attention kernel for the customer's pool to SDPA or force fallback. I can patch routing to a pool with REDWOOD_FLASHATTN=0 while we investigate.
Nora: reproduce steps I used earlier for a similar report:
```
# repro script
python perf_repro.py --model redwood-3b-embed --seq_len 1536 --batch 1 --tokens 1536 --iters 50
# prints latency percentiles
```
Nora: local numbers with kernel-v1.8 (pre-roll): p95=120ms p99=200ms
Nora: with kernel-v1.9-ffa3c + FlashAttention enabled: p95=140ms p99=650ms (huge tail)
Alex: can you paste the perf log?
Nora: sure:
```
# perf output excerpt
seq=1536 iters=50
median=110ms p95=140ms p99=650ms
CPU mem=12G GPU mem spike ~80% at iter 30 (KV cache churn observed)
stack: flash_attn_cuda_kernel.cu:line 412
```
Michael: KV cache churn makes sense — FlashAttention sometimes changes memory access patterns and causes higher warp occupancy for certain seq lengths. That plus our kernel selection heuristic might be choosing FlashAttn when SDPA would be cheaper for long sequences.
Sara: two parallel tracks: 1) short term mitigation (route affected tenant away from FlashAttn) 2) root cause — fix kernel selection heuristic or patch FlashAttn kernel.
Matt: I created a quick routing override: set pool annotation attention_kernel=sdpa for acme-prod. infra-bot created change request CR-8902. Will do a canary shift of 10% traffic now.
infra-bot: Rollout started: CR-8902, 10% -> 50% -> 100% canary, estimated 12m per stage.
support-bot: Notified customer that we are investigating and applying a mitigation (routing their traffic to SDPA pool).
Alex: for debugging I'll compile a debug build with these flags to toggle kernels at runtime: -DUSE_FLASH_ATTENTION -DLOG_ATTENTION_SELECTION. Can we get a perf trace from the customer's host?
Michael: support already uploaded a few traces. I'll put them in the shared bucket.
Nora: quick note from local profiling: FlashAttn kernel has worse latency variance for seq>1024 when batch=1; SDPA is more bandwidth-friendly for long sequences. Also our kernel selector threshold was tuned on typical seq=256 workloads — not long tails.
Sara: propose we change selector to prefer SDPA for seq>=768 for embed model family as a stopgap, and add a perf test to CI for seq 1536 batch 1.
Matt: agreed. I'll push a runtime config override so we can change threshold without redeploy. Patch MR pending: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/patches/1234
Alex: longer term: upstream FlashAttention team has an optimization for KV cache friendly memory layout. We can try their patch or add our own kernel fallback when memory spike detected. I'll open an issue.
Michael: action items: 
- Matt: finish routing rollback to SDPA for acme (in progress)
- Sara/Alex: add CI perf test for long-seq single batch and update selector heuristic
- Nora: run controlled A/B to confirm p99 drop after routing switch
- Infra-bot: track CR-8902 and post completion

Matt: can confirm canary at 10% shows p99 falling back to ~190-220ms for the sampled traffic. Waiting 15m to promote.
oncall: monitoring alert rule tuned — raising slack alert on p99>=400ms for emb endpoints.
support-bot: customer msg: "Thanks, noticed immediate improvement during canary. Awaiting full rollout." :thumbsup:
Alex: I'll try reproducing with ASAN/UBSAN disabled builds to rule out subtle mem issues, and test upstream FlashAttn commit a1b2c3.
Nora: logging note: added extra attention selection logs under DEBUG so we can see which kernel was chosen per request (will expire after 24h).
Michael: prefer we keep routing change for acme until selector/patch is validated. If tests look good we can change default heuristic and remove override.
Sara: timeline — aim to have selector change + CI test in 24-48h, patch to runtime config in next deploy, and rollback override removed after 1-2 days of stable telemetry.
Matt: will update CR-8902 with canary metrics.
Alex: opened issue: https://git.redwood/repo/eng-runtime/issues/456 "FlashAttn p99 regressions for long-seq workloads" with repro script and perf logs.
Michael: thanks folks. keeping this thread as single source for the escalation. I'll post final status once CR-8902 completes and we validate p99 is back to baseline.
Nora: final note — added a short checklist for Support to gather in future: model, quantization, seq_len distribution, batch sizes, sample request ids, kernel build hash, sysinfo. Saves time.
support-bot: checklist template posted to #support-templates.
Matt: canary promoted to 100% at 1759990105. infra-bot: Rollout success.
infra-bot: CR-8902 completed.
Michael: customer confirmed full fix, p99 back to baseline. closing escalation. :tada:
